original_question: If one ranges over all smooth 4-manifolds homeomorphic to S^2 x S^2, rather than fixing the standard smooth manifold itself, must every complex structure on such a manifold come from an even Hirzebruch surface, or can there exist other complex surfaces homeomorphic to S^2 x S^2?
target_in_paper: Section 6, Problem 25: "Determine all complex structures of S^2 × S^2." The immediately following discussion isolates the remaining open part as the case of compact complex surfaces whose underlying smooth 4-manifold is only homeomorphic, not necessarily diffeomorphic, to S^2 × S^2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1305.4623))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the unresolved variant emphasized by Kotschick: once one ranges over smooth 4-manifolds homeomorphic to S^2 × S^2, the question becomes whether there can be complex surfaces other than the even Hirzebruch surfaces. It also correctly contrasts this with the already-settled case of the standard smooth structure. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1305.4623))
missing_details: The paper’s official formulation is broader and should be named explicitly: Problem 25 itself asks to determine all complex structures of S^2 × S^2, not only the homeomorphic-variant extracted from the later discussion. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1305.4623))

To be fully stand-alone, the question should say "compact complex surface" (equivalently, a complex structure on a compact smooth 4-manifold), since the paper is discussing complex structures in real dimension 4 / complex dimension 2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1305.4623))

The category distinction should be stated explicitly: for the standard smooth manifold S^2 × S^2, hence for any complex surface diffeomorphic to it, the only possibilities are the even Hirzebruch surfaces; the open case begins only when one allows manifolds merely homeomorphic to S^2 × S^2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1305.4623))

The comparison class should be identified as the even Hirzebruch surfaces, which the paper notes already give infinitely many non-biholomorphic complex Kähler structures on S^2 × S^2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1305.4623))

The nearby classification argument should be incorporated if one wants the sharpest paper-faithful formulation: any compact complex surface with the Betti numbers and the intersection form of S^2 × S^2 is Kähler, projective algebraic, minimal, and therefore either a Hirzebruch surface or a minimal surface of general type. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1305.4623))

Ambient ring/field, variables, operators, homogeneity, degree restrictions, nilpotency conditions, and "for all sufficiently large m"-type quantifiers are not applicable here; the hidden assumptions instead concern compactness, complex-surface dimension, homeomorphism type, smooth structure, and classification up to biholomorphism. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1305.4623))
refined_question: Determine all complex structures on the smooth 4-manifold S^2 × S^2: equivalently, since the only compact complex surfaces diffeomorphic to the standard smooth S^2 × S^2 are the even Hirzebruch surfaces, must every compact complex surface homeomorphic to S^2 × S^2 be biholomorphic to an even Hirzebruch surface, or can there exist a non-Hirzebruch complex surface on a manifold homeomorphic but not diffeomorphic to S^2 × S^2? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1305.4623))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, does there exist a compact complex surface homeomorphic to S^2 × S^2 that is a minimal surface of general type, or does that homeomorphism type force the surface to be a Hirzebruch surface? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1305.4623))
justification: This draft is targeting Section 6, Problem 25, not the neighboring problems about complex structures on projective spaces. The paper is organized by Hirzebruch problem numbers rather than by a Conjecture 1.1 / Proposition 1.2 / Theorem 1.3 format, and the nearest official wording is exactly "Determine all complex structures of S^2 × S^2." Kotschick then immediately explains the point your draft is trying to capture: the standard smooth-structure case is settled, but the version allowing manifolds only homeomorphic to S^2 × S^2 remains open. The following classification discussion is what makes the alternate formulation via minimal surfaces of general type legitimate and paper-faithful. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1305.4623))
